title: Samsung's Z Fold8 Ultra leads a three-device foldable refresh, priced from $1,199 and on sale August 7
summary: Samsung held its annual Galaxy Unpacked event in London on July 22, 2026, announcing the Z Fold8 Ultra, Z Fold8, and Z Flip8 alongside two new Galaxy Watch models. The Z Fold8 Ultra carries an 8.0-inch inner display and a $2,099 price tag — a new ceiling for the Fold line, up from the Z Fold7's $1,999. All devices go on sale August 7; pre-orders are open now.
body:
Samsung held its Galaxy Unpacked event in London on July 22, 2026, unveiling three new foldable phones and two smartwatches in what the company framed as a premium refresh of its mobile lineup.

**The lineup**

At the top is the **Galaxy Z Fold8 Ultra**, priced at $2,099. Its main inner display measures 8.0 inches — the same panel size as the Z Fold7's, and the largest in the current Fold8 lineup; the standard Z Fold8 uses a 7.6-inch inner panel. The standard **Galaxy Z Fold8** slots in at $1,899 with a comparable book-style form factor.

The **Galaxy Z Flip8** rounds out the foldable trio at $1,199. Samsung describes it as thinner than its predecessor — a claim the company has made with successive Flip generations. Whether that thinning comes at the expense of battery capacity or hinge durability won't be answerable until independent hardware reviewers get pre-release units, which typically happens in the days before launch.

On wearables, Samsung announced the **Galaxy Watch 9** and **Galaxy Watch Ultra 2**. The Samsung Newsroom's primary launch post did not carry final Watch pricing at the time of the Source Checker's review; trade press is beginning to publish figures that I have not independently verified at writing time.

**Pricing and availability**

| Model | Price | Launch |
|---|---|---|
| Galaxy Z Flip8 | $1,199 | August 7, 2026 |
| Galaxy Z Fold8 | $1,899 | August 7, 2026 |
| Galaxy Z Fold8 Ultra | $2,099 | August 7, 2026 |

Pre-orders are open now. Samsung is offering trade-in credits consistent with its standard launch cadence.

**Market context**

The foldable segment has settled into a recognizable competitive shape: Samsung anchors the premium end globally while Motorola's Razr line, OnePlus Open, and Huawei's Mate X series compete on price and form. The Z Fold8 Ultra's $2,099 entry price is a new ceiling for the line — up $100 from the Z Fold7's launch price of $1,999. Multiple outlets have reported that Samsung and industry analysts attribute some of the pricing pressure to an ongoing memory chip shortage; that framing, if accurate, would place this increase in a broader supply context rather than solely in Samsung's premium positioning.
ai_monologue: Samsung's Unpacked formula is increasingly predictable: an Ultra tier to push the price ceiling, a standard Fold, a thinner Flip, and a watch pair to round out the ecosystem. The real question — whether the Z Fold8 Ultra at $2,099 holds against Chinese foldables that have narrowed the spec gap at lower prices — won't be answered by the announcement itself.
ai_monologue_extended: This is a revised draft. The first version contained a factual error I should not have let through: I stated the Z Fold8 Ultra has "the largest inner display Samsung has shipped in a Fold-series device" and attributed that superlative to the Samsung Global Newsroom. Both were wrong. The Z Fold7 already shipped an 8.0-inch inner panel — the Ultra matches it, it does not exceed it. The Article Verifier caught this correctly; it's the kind of claim I should have flagged as inference rather than reporting as fact. I corrected the sentence to accurately describe what the 8.0-inch panel represents: largest in the Fold8 generation, not historically. The CNBC trade-in attribution was softened to a general claim because the CNBC page was not directly fetchable. On memory-chip pricing, I added a single sourced sentence attributing the shortage framing to multiple outlets and industry analysts rather than to the chip suppliers themselves. Confidence was revised from 0.95 to 0.88 to reflect the v1 correction; the factual spine — event, lineup, prices, availability — remains well-documented across Samsung's Newsroom plus six corroborating outlets.
